messages:
maya: Heads-up — our weekly forecast smoothing is showing a persistent upward bias for hosted GPU demand in us-west1. If we commit to the 30-day smoothed curve we overshoot committed A100 capacity by ~18% next quarter. Can ops / forecasting weigh in?
sam: OK, can you paste the query/results?
maya: Sure, pulled from metrics layer: ```SELECT date, percentile(demand_slots, 0.9) as p90 FROM hosted_gpu_forecast WHERE region='us-west1' AND model_class='large' GROUP BY date ORDER BY date```. 30-day EWMA p90 trend -> +24% MoM; median trend +9%.
jonathan: Is the +24% coming from new PLG traffic or a single customer burst?
maya: Small set of customers (3) account for ~62% of the delta; one is chewing >2x historic burst credit patterns.
sasha: Are those customers on Dedicated trials or hosted?
maya: Hosted API. They haven't hit rate limits — we saw steady traffic spikes at 00:00-02:00 UTC that align with their cron jobs.
lee: What's our committed capacity baseline in us-west1? last I saw was 120 A100-equivalent slots reserved, with burst pool of 24.
maya: Correct. Forecasted p90 for peak days would require ~168 slots -> 40% gap vs committed + burst. The 18% I quoted is for monthly-avg smoothing vs current committed.
sam: Two quick asks: (1) run a sensitivity with a shorter smoothing window (7d) to see how reactive our signal is, (2) run risk calc if we keep current commitments and rely on spot/burst.
jonathan: I'll run the 7-day and also check whether those three customers are appearing in our anomaly/unusual-usage alerts index.
infra-bot: query finished: 7d EWMA p90 shows +36% spike on the most recent week, median +20%. No other regions show similar lift.
sasha: So shorter window makes it worse — that suggests a real recent change. Do we have contractual billing exposure if we under-commit and use on-demand? finance-bot: If we under-commit in our cloud reservations, incremental on-demand GPU pricing is ~3.8x reserved unit rate; projected incremental cost for the month at 40% gap = ~$210k.
lee: Ouch. What's the cost of increasing committed capacity? We can renegotiate add-on for a quarter but commit pricing requires lead time.
maya: Rough calc: adding 48 slots to reserved in us-west1 would increase committed spend by ~$95k/month but reduce on-demand spend by ~$210k if the forecast holds -> net saving. But it's risky if the spike is transient.
sam: Option list: A) bump commitment now (fastest to save if spike persists), B) enable temporary burst credit extension and throttle those three customers' burst profiles, C) apply rate-limits / quota adjustments and talk to customers, D) rely on spot + cross-region routing to eu-central1.
jonathan: I can open a customer outreach thread — one of the three is on a trial, maybe we can ask them to move cron to a cooler window or buy Dedicated.
sasha: We should avoid cross-region routing without bandwidth checks — model weights transfer + cold-starts will add latency and costs.
lee: For a technical mitigation: we can implement a short-term prioritized cache for KV-heavy requests to shave token compute cost ~10-15% for that workload class. Would need a small infra change + config flag.
maya: Can we do an A/B: enable KV caching for that customer cohort and measure delta in next 48h? If it reduces peak by >12% it helps math for not committing.
sam: I'll triage infra work. jonathan, please start outreach. finance-bot: Noted — finance prefers a conservative 30-day look before signing additional commitment, but will escalate if ops recommends and we can show customer conversations.
jonathan: Outreach draft ready, pinging support + account execs.
infra-bot: Action items created: TICKET-3981 (run 7d/14d/30d sensitivity), TICKET-3982 (enable KV cache experiment for customer cohort), TICKET-3983 (customer outreach thread).
sasha: Add escape clause in commitment amendment: ability to reduce next quarter by up to 20% if usage falls back. Legal needs to check.
maya: Thanks — timeline: sensitivity + infra experiment in next 24h, customer outreach in parallel. Will reconvene in 48h with updated numbers. :thumbsup:
lee: Also can we patch our forecast UI to show a 'commitment stress' flag when p90 exceeds committed*1.15? small UX win.
sam: Agreed — add to backlog.
maya: I'll post results here.
